messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: KV cache paged metadata growth detected in us-east-1 serving pool. Spike started ~2112345600. Affected service: continuous-batcher / block-manager. Auto-triggered mitigation: throttling QPS on tier=free.

oncall-jay: seeing it — traces show steady increase in block metadata size, not evicting fast enough. tailing /var/log/blockmgr.log now.

anika: logs: `block_manager:evict_loop` stuck with repeated OOM-ish drops, but OOM isn't being raised. Suspect metadata leak in paged index.

kevin: observed metrics: meta_entries_count +260% in 6m; metadata-alloc rate 12GB/min, blockstore write lat spiked. CPU on block-manager pods at 90%.

maria: customer impact? any 5xxs or latency cliffs?

oncall-jay: yes, a few P95 generation spikes to ~2.8s for requests using long context. Some customers reported timeouts. Support ticket surge flagged: 7 tickets in last 10m.

support-lena: listing affected customers from support queue: acme-inc, petite-ai, internal-sandbox-3. Marking acme-inc as high-priority.

eng-runtime-oya: quick mitigations to try: 1) reduce continuous-batch window to 30ms, 2) disable KV prefetcher, 3) increase eviction aggressiveness by lowering block_lifetime to 10s. Can roll as config flags, no binary change.

anika: can we push (2) and (3) asap? (1) affects throughput but should reduce metadata pressure.

oncall-jay: I'll push config change to canary pool first (us-east-1a). Command: ```kubectl patch cm blockmgr-config -n runtime -p '{"data":{"prefetch.enabled":"false","evict.block_lifetime_s":"10","continuous_batch.ms":"30"}}'```

kevin: also recommend enabling block_manager debug sampling on one pod: ```curl -X POST http://blockmgr-0:9000/debug?sample_meta=1``` to capture extra metadata keys for postmortem.

oncall-jay: canary patch applied to us-east-1a -> patch success on 3/3 pods. Monitoring now.

anika: immediate effect visible: meta_entries_count dropping on canary - 40% in 90s. CPU on patched pods down 25%.

maria: rolling to remaining pools with throttle: we should keep free-tier QPS throttle until stable. Support, prepare a short incident notice for affected customers.

support-lena: drafting message: "We're investigating elevated request latencies for some long-context requests. We're applying mitigations; we'll update in 30m." tagging acme-inc.

eng-runtime-oya: temporary routing change to divert high-QPS customers away from paged-KV nodes: updating routing policy to prefer unpaged-models for heavy queries. Patch in router config: `route.prefer_unpaged=true` for top-20 qps clients.

oncall-jay: routing change applied. Should reduce ingress to paged nodes by ~18%.

kevin: after full roll, meta_entries_count stabilized across pools, overall metadata allocation rate back to baseline in 10m. Looks like prefetcher + continuous batching interaction was causing supersets of metadata to be materialized.

anika: root cause hypothesis: prefetcher request pattern + enlarged continuous batch window allowed many near-identical prefixes to populate paged KV metadata before eviction could complete, causing a metadata blowup. Also found a bug where eviction counter wasn't incremented for partially paged blocks -> leak.

maria: action items: 1) hotfix: revert prefetcher + tighten batch window (done), 2) patch block_manager to fix eviction counter bug (code PR), 3) add regression test for metadata accounting, 4) customer follow-up.

oncall-jay: handing off to eng-runtime pager for long-form fix. @eng-runtime-oya you're up for next 6 hours?

eng-runtime-oya: taking it. I'll open PR for eviction-counter fix and schedule canary. Also collecting heapdumps and meta-sampling data to attach to PR.

anika: please include repro harness for continuous-batcher with prefetcher on long-context sequences. Will add a unit/regression test.

support-lena: sent initial customer note to acme-inc and petite-ai. Both acknowledged and asked for ETA; gave tentative 2-4 hours for full fix + postmortem.

oncall-jay: summary for handoff: mitigations applied (prefetcher off, batch window 30ms, block_lifetime 10s, routing pref to unpaged nodes for heavy clients). Monitor panels: blockmgr.meta_entries_count, blockmgr.evict_rate, continuous_batch.latency_p95.

kevin: recommend post-incident knobs: add automatic circuit-breaker to disable prefetcher when meta growth exceeds threshold, and an alert for eviction_counter_delta==0 for >30s.

anika: agreed. I'll file infra ticket and include as follow-up in incident doc.

oncall-jay: tagging for follow-up: @maria to own customer comms, @anika to own code fix, @kevin to own alerts, @oya for canary and heap dumps.

eng-runtime-oya: capturing logs and heapdumps now. Will upload to incident artifact bucket and link in the postmortem.

maria: I'll coordinate postmortem and schedule 1hr blameless review tomorrow 15:00UTC.

oncall-jay: handing to next on-call in 2h. All clear for now? Keep pager active for regressions. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations successful, impact reduced to low. Monitoring will continue for 3 hours. Incident severity set to SEV-2.

eng-runtime-oya: final note before I start deeper debugging: reproduce workload script attached in artifacts. If anyone needs immediate debug access, DM me.

oncall-jay: thanks team. Handoff complete.
